los.text: Describe the appropriate sizing and insertion technique for a laryngeal mask airway (LMA).
los.html:
StepDetail
Sizing (by weight)
  • Size 3: 30–50 kg (small adult)
  • Size 4: 50–70 kg
  • Size 5: 70–100 kg (as a rule, 4 for women, 5 for men)
CheckInflate and deflate the cuff, lubricate the back
PositionHead in "sniffing the morning air" (if no C-spine concern)
Insert
  • Cuff deflated, open side facing the tongue
  • Press along the hard palate with the index finger, advance until resistance (it sits over the laryngeal inlet)
InflateWith the recommended air volume (or use an i-gel: no cuff, self-sealing)
ConfirmChest rise, breath sounds, capnography (end-tidal CO₂)
SecureTape or tie
  • LMA = supraglottic airway device: easier than intubation; used in cardiac arrest and anaesthesia.

los.text: Identify contraindications for the use of a laryngeal mask airway.
los.html:
ContraindicationReason
Gag reflex present / not deeply unconsciousVomiting, laryngospasm
High aspiration risk (full stomach, bowel obstruction, late pregnancy)Doesn't protect against aspiration
Upper airway obstruction or trauma (below or at the larynx), oral traumaMay not seal or may worsen
Limited mouth openingCan't insert
Need for high airway pressures (stiff lungs, severe bronchospasm)Leak

los.text: Describe the principles and basic steps of tracheal intubation.
los.html:
1. PrepareTeam roles, equipment checked (laryngoscope, tubes in two sizes, bougie, suction, capnography), monitoring, IV access, drugs, plan B (supraglottic, front-of-neck access).
2Pre-oxygenate with 100% oxygen for 3 minutes.
3Induction and paralysis (rapid sequence induction if aspiration risk).
4. PositionSniffing position, laryngoscope in the right of the mouth, sweep the tongue left, lift (don't lever) to see the vocal cords.
5Pass the endotracheal tube through the cords (cuff just below), inflate the cuff.
6. ConfirmWaveform capnography (gold standard), chest rise, breath sounds both sides, not over the stomach.
7Secure; ventilate; CXR for tube position.
  • Advantage: definitive airway that protects against aspiration; "No trace = wrong place".

los.text: Explain the different types of inhalers, their indications, and demonstrate correct inhaler technique.
los.html:
InhalerExamplesTechnique key points
pMDI (pressurised metered dose)Salbutamol, beclometasone
  • Shake, breathe out, seal lips, press and breathe in slowly and deeply, hold breath 10 s
  • Use a spacer (better delivery, children, acute attacks)
Dry powder inhaler (DPI)Turbohaler, Accuhaler, ElliptaLoad, breathe out away from it, breathe in quickly and deeply, hold 10 s; don't shake or exhale into it
Soft mistRespimatSlow inhalation
NebuliserSalbutamol, ipratropiumAcute severe attacks, unable to use inhalers
TypeUse
SABA (salbutamol)Reliever
ICS (beclometasone, budesonide)Preventer (asthma); rinse mouth (oral thrush)
LABA (formoterol, salmeterol)With ICS only in asthma
ICS/formoterol (MART, AIR)Reliever and preventer in one (BTS/NICE/SIGN 2024)
LAMA (tiotropium)COPD, add-on in asthma
  • Check technique at every review before stepping up treatment.

los.text: Explain the clinical indications for requesting an arterial blood gas (ABG) test.
los.html:
IndicationInformation gained
Respiratory failure (low sats, drowsiness, COPD exacerbation)PaO₂, PaCO₂: type 1 vs type 2 respiratory failure
Acid–base disturbance: DKA, sepsis, renal failure, poisoningpH, HCO₃⁻, base excess, lactate
Severe asthmaRising or normal CO₂ = life-threatening
ShockLactate
Rapid electrolytes, Hb, glucose, carboxyhaemoglobinPoint-of-care values
Ventilated / NIV patientsAdjust settings
  • Venous gas is enough for pH, bicarbonate, lactate and potassium; arterial is needed for oxygenation.

los.text: Demonstrate the ability to perform an arterial blood gas sampling on a model, applying aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) principles throughout the procedure.
los.html:
1Check indication; Allen's test (collateral ulnar flow) before radial puncture; check anticoagulation, platelets.
2Explain (it's more painful than venepuncture), consent; note oxygen therapy (FiO₂).
3
  • ANTT: hand hygiene, gloves, clean the skin over the radial artery (proximal to the wrist crease, lateral to FCR), allow to dry
  • Local anaesthetic if time.
4. Heparinised syringe
  • Expel excess
  • Palpate the pulse with two fingers
  • Insert at 30–45° bevel up
  • Towards the pulse
  • Until arterial blood pulsates into the syringe (1–2 mL).
5Withdraw and press firmly for 5 minutes (longer if anticoagulated).
6Expel air bubbles, cap, mix, label, analyse within 10–15 minutes (or on ice).
7Sharps disposal, document site, time, FiO₂; check the hand perfusion.

los.text: Perform a rapid A to E assessment of a patient presenting with shortness of breath, demonstrating the ability to identify key clinical signs, prioritise interventions, and make appropriate clinical decisions to manage the patient's condition.
los.html:
StageAcute asthma findingsAction
ATalking?—
BPEF % best/predicted, can't complete sentences, RR ≥25, silent chest, sats <92%, cyanosis, exhaustionOxygen to 94–98%, salbutamol 5 mg nebulised (back-to-back), ipratropium 500 µg
CHR ≥110, hypotension, arrhythmiaIV access, bloods
DConfusion, drowsinessABG: normal or raised CO₂ = life-threatening
ETriggers (infection, allergens)Prednisolone 40–50 mg (or IV hydrocortisone 100 mg)
SeverityFeatures
ModeratePEF 50–75%
Acute severePEF 33–50%, RR ≥25, HR ≥110, can't complete sentences
Life-threateningPEF <33%, sats <92%, PaO₂ <8 kPa, normal PaCO₂, silent chest, cyanosis, poor effort, exhaustion, arrhythmia, hypotension, confusion
Near-fatalRaised PaCO₂ or needing ventilation
  • Escalate: senior and ICU early; IV magnesium 2 g over 20 min if poor response.
